key_insight: Electrically Assisted Friction Stir Welding (EAFSW) adds localized electrical heating to conventional FSW to reduce flow stress, cutting forces and torque while expanding the range of weldable materials.
engineering_relevance: EAFSW is a practical route to join high-strength and hard-to-weld metals with lower tool wear, higher welding speed, and improved process efficiency.
method: Feed electric current into the rotating tool and/or workpiece
Use Joule heating and possible electroplastic softening ahead of the tool
Tune electrode design, circuit layout, and electrical parameters to control force/torque response
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes reported experimental and numerical results across aluminum, magnesium, titanium, steel, dissimilar joints, and composites, comparing EAFSW with other auxiliary-energy FSW variants.
watch_item: Adoption is constrained by current distribution control, electrode wear, arcing risk, safety requirements, and added system cost.
paper_title: The Effect of Auxiliary Electrical Energy Engineering Friction Stir Welding Technology (EAFSW): A Review
